records.title: NSP1-SAMD9L interactions govern murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo.
records.abstract: Rotavirus replication, pathogenesis, and transmission are host-range restricted, yet the viral and host determinants remain poorly defined. Rotavirus nonstructural protein 1 (NSP1) is a multifunctional innate immune antagonist dispensable for replication in permissive cells. Here, using reverse genetics, neonatal mice, intestinal organoids, and comparative proteomics, we identify mouse SAMD9L as a critical host restriction factor selectively antagonized by murine rotavirus-encoded NSP1. An NSP1-deletion murine-like rotavirus produced progeny efficiently in cell lines but was highly attenuated in neonatal mice with no productive intestinal replication, fecal shedding, and diarrhea. Recombinant monoreassortant viruses carrying NSP1 genes from rhesus, bovine, or human rotavirus strains did not support murine intestinal infection, even in Stat1-/- pups, indicating an additional restriction mechanism beyond STAT1-dependent antiviral signaling. Comparative proteomics identified mouse SAMD9L as a specific interactor of murine NSP1, and NSP1 promoted SAMD9L degradation through a neddylation- and proteasome-dependent pathway. AlphaFold3 guided mutagenesis identified NSP1 residues S364/E366 and SAMD9L residues R455/L462 as functionally important for the NSP1-SAMD9L interaction. Mutations on either side disrupted NSP1-SAMD9L association and prevented SAMD9L degradation. Replication of murine rotaviruses carrying S364A or E366A mutations was undetectable in wild-type mice and was restored in Samd9l-/- mice. Combined deletion of Samd9l and Stat1 permitted replication of otherwise attenuated viruses carrying mismatched NSP1s and enabled fecal IgA seroconversion after a single oral inoculation of Rotarix. These findings identify SAMD9L as a physiologically relevant intestinal restriction factor in mice and show that murine NSP1 antagonism of mouse SAMD9L contributes to murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo.

records.title: Protocol to isolate and culture progenitor cells of airway submucosal glands from human proximal airways.
records.abstract: The airway submucosal glands (SMGs) are an important component of the airways, as they contribute to mucus production, antimicrobial defense, and epithelial repair, yet they are often absent from in vitro respiratory models. Here, we present a protocol for isolating and culturing SMG progenitor cells from human proximal airways. We describe steps for tissue dissociation and generation of SMG epithelial organoids and surface airway epithelial (SAE) organoids. We also include characterization steps using RT-qPCR, immunocytochemistry, and ELISA for validation.

records.title: High-throughput screening of patient iPSC-derived neurons identifies the gut microbial metabolites that attenuate Alzheimer's disease pathology.
records.abstract: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites influence the gut-brain axis and may impact Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology. However, the microbial metabolites involved in this process and their functional roles are largely unknown. We screened 352 gut metabolites in induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC)-derived neurons from individuals with AD to identify compounds that reduce tau hyperphosphorylation. We identified agmatine as a lead candidate, which decreased hyperphosphorylated tau in neurons and cerebral organoids. In 5xFAD mice, agmatine (100 mg/kg/day) improved cognition, reduced amyloid plaques, lowered neuroinflammation, and increased beneficial gut bacteria, including Agathobacter and Bacteroides. Transcriptomic analysis showed that agmatine downregulated complement and inflammatory genes (C1QB, C2, C3AR1, CCL3, CXCL8, and CXCL6) in patient iPSC-derived cerebral organoids. Agmatine also decreased C3aR and pSTAT3 levels in vivo, mechanistically supporting the reduced tau phosphorylation in iPSC-derived neurons. Altogether, these findings identified the therapeutic potential of gut-derived metabolites and identified agmatine as potential treatment for AD.

records.title: Directional Group B Streptococcus Infection Differentially Shapes Cytokine Signaling across the Placental Maternal-Fetal Interface.
records.abstract: Placentitis involves spatially complex interactions between pathogens and distinct cellular layers of the placenta, yet current experimental models fail to capture the directional nature of these infection dynamics. Understanding how infection directionality shapes compartment-specific immune responses across the placental maternal-fetal interface is critical for identifying early biomarkers and therapeutic targets for preterm birth. In this study, we used a placental maternal-fetal interface organ-on-a-chip (OoC) model that structurally mimics the maternal-fetal interface within the placenta to investigate immunologic responses induced by Group B Streptococcus (GBS) infection, including effects of infection directionality across the maternal-fetal interface. The OoC model consisted of decidual and cytotrophoblast chambers with and without macrophages. In the OoC model, release of IL-1β, IL-6, MMP-9, and TNF-α was most pronounced from the cytotrophoblast chamber. Addition of THP-1 macrophage-like cells to either chamber led to no significant differences between MMP-9 and IL-1β release between the chambers. The OoC model demonstrates chamber specific differences with respect to immune signaling with the cytotrophoblast chamber driving inflammatory signaling at the placental maternal-fetal interface. These findings support the potential of OoC platforms for studying placentitis while highlighting the need for further model optimization.

records.title: Role of Bile Acids in Colorectal Diseases.
records.abstract: Bile acids (BAs) have functions well beyond fat digestion. They also serve as signals linking the gut microbiota to gut health. This review examines how BAs affect colorectal diseases and how this knowledge can guide diagnosis and treatment. BAs and gut bacteria shape each other, and this balance affects the gut lining, immune system, and inflammation. Problems in BA handling are linked to bile acid diarrhea, post-cholecystectomy diarrhea, microscopic colitis, irritable bowel syndrome, inflammatory bowel disease, and colorectal cancer. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry and organoid models enable faster, more detailed BA testing. New treatments include BA binders, farnesoid X receptor-targeting drugs, and engineered gut bacteria. BAs play a central role in many colorectal diseases through their effects on gut bacteria and the gut lining. Better BA testing can improve diagnosis, and new BA- and microbiota-based treatments show promise. More studies are needed to bring these approaches into clinical practice.

records.title: Targeting PI3K signalling for broad inhibition of β-Coronavirus infection.
records.abstract: The phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) signalling pathway plays a central role in regulating key cellular processes such as survival, metabolism, and immune responses. Aberrant activation of this pathway is associated with tumorigenesis, and several PI3K inhibitors have been developed as anticancer agents. Emerging evidence suggests that viruses, including β-coronaviruses, have evolved mechanisms to exploit host PI3K signalling for their replication and immune evasion. In this study, we evaluated the antiviral efficacy of a panel of PI3K inhibitors against β-coronaviruses, including murine hepatitis virus (MHV), human OC43 (HuCoV-OC43) and four major SARS-CoV-2 variants using both cell line and organoid models. Our findings reveal that these compounds exhibit low micromolar potency in inhibiting viral replication. Notably, the PI3K/mTOR inhibitor C20 (PWT33597) demonstrated broad-spectrum activity against multiple β-coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, MHV, and HuCoV-OC43, in conventional cell lines and in air-liquid interface (ALI)-cultured, differentiated primary human bronchial epithelial cells. Given that cytokine storm is a major contributor to SARS-CoV-2-related multi-organ failure and mortality, we further explored the impact of PI3K inhibition on host inflammatory responses. We found that MHV infection markedly increased cytokine expression in RAW264.7 macrophages. Interestingly, treatment with C20 further amplified cytokine production, suggesting complex immunomodulatory effects that may not be universally beneficial. Together, our findings indicate that PI3K inhibitors such as C20 exhibit promising broad-spectrum antiviral activity. Although their immunomodulatory effects, such as enhanced cytokine production, warrant further investigation, these compounds may offer a dual opportunity to fine-tune both antiviral and host immune responses with appropriate therapeutic strategies.

records.title: Virtual Knockout in the Era of Generative AI: From Intracellular Networks to Spatial and Cross-Modal Functional Simulations.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation data have enabled computational models that predict intervention-associated cellular responses. This narrative review organizes explicit gene-regulatory-network simulations, latent and compositional response models, graph, optimal-transport, and dynamical approaches, foundation-model representations, and emerging spatial or cross-modal settings through a virtual-knockout lens. We distinguish representation-level ablation from causal genetic intervention and separate held-out regimes for genes, cell types or contexts, perturbation combinations, chemical structures, and doses. We compare representative methods, experimental resources, metrics, and benchmark frameworks and operationally define a prospective holographic virtual cell by its modalities, regulatory and physical constraints, intervention-conditioned outputs with calibrated uncertainty, and prospective validation requirements. The holographic virtual cell and Design-Build-Test-Learn roadmap are presented as future-facing criteria rather than as an achieved clinical capability.

records.title: Engineering of Microbial Cell Factories for Flavonoid Production: from Flavanone Platforms to Tailored Derivatives.
records.abstract: Flavonoids are valuable plant polyphenols used in foods, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. However, their production is limited by the low abundance of many flavonoids in plants and the structural complexity that complicates chemical synthesis. Microbial cell factories provide a sustainable alternative, yet engineering requirements increase sharply from platform flavanones to oxidized and multiply tailored derivatives. This Review organizes recent advances according to product complexity, covering flavanones, oxidized flavones and flavonols, and methylated, glycosylated, and prenylated flavonoids. We examine the major constraints at each product level, including aromatic precursor and malonyl-CoA supply, enzyme activity and selectivity, redox and oxygen demands, and the regeneration of activated methyl, sugar, and prenyl donors. We further highlight the need to coordinate scaffold formation, oxidation, tailoring reactions, donor regeneration, and host metabolism rather than optimizing individual pathway steps independently. Finally, emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategies for enzyme engineering, demand-responsive pathway regulation, automated design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycles, and virtual-cell modeling are discussed. This product-complexity-oriented framework provides design principles for developing efficient, modular, and programmable microbial platforms for flavonoid biomanufacturing.

records.title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction.
records.abstract: Foundation-model predictors of perturbation response are evaluated primarily by aggregate accuracy. Using their predictions to prioritize experiments requires assessing each prediction's reliability. We audit the state-transition (ST) decoder used in STATE across three encoders (SE-600M, scGPT, and Tahoe-x1) and four cell lines under CRISPRi. The decoder's first attention layer has a low-rank output. Projecting this output onto 4-32 fixed directions estimated from training activations preserves mean per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC). This low-rank attention bottleneck bounds the decoder's reliability by distance to training responses: PDC declines as the cosine distance from a perturbation's observed response to its nearest training response increases. We propose predicted-NN-distance, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, as a per-prediction confidence score. The score has a mean absolute Spearman correlation of 0.81 with PDC, close to the 0.88 obtained with the observed response. Thresholds calibrated on this score transfer across encoders and cell lines, and the score remains predictive of PDC for drug perturbations.

records.title: LeakageHunter-SCFM: Evidence-bounded dataset-lineage auditing for single-cell foundation model benchmarks.
records.abstract: To develop and evaluate LeakageHunter-SCFM, an evidence-bounded informatics framework for auditing dataset-lineage evidence and calibrating benchmark-independence claims in single-cell foundation model evaluation. LeakageHunter-SCFM extracts accessions, DOIs, URLs, and repository identifiers from manuscripts and related artifacts. The workflow canonicalizes resources, assigns dataset roles, constructs candidate overlap pairs, and applies claim ceilings before reviewer adjudication. We evaluated it in a curated development corpus, a locked retrospective external evaluation set, and a small prediction-blinded prospective proof-of-concept evaluation. The development workflow reduced 673 raw candidates to 84 filtered resource entries and 53 candidate overlap pairs. Prediction-visible reviewer forms agreed across all 140 retrospective evidence units; their historical labels yielded F1 0.842 across 132 binary-scored units. Independent prediction-blinded relabeling of all 140 units followed by third-assessor adjudication yielded precision 0.727, recall 0.667, specificity 0.910, and F1 0.696 across 136 binary-scored units. The seven-record, prediction-blinded proof of concept achieved recall 1.000 and precision 0.611 across 52 evidence units. All actionable-positive units came from one record. Restricting this analysis to full article bodies retained 50 units from five records and F1 0.759. Evidence-bounded lineage auditing supports biomedical foundation-model benchmark review by separating identifier overlap, actionable review priority, and confirmed exposure. LeakageHunter-SCFM provides a reproducible triage layer for lineage evidence and reserves claims about corpus membership and performance effects for direct supporting evidence.

records.title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.
records.abstract: Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses. This review introduces a nested framework of six capabilities for AI-powered virtual cells, spanning population-derived models, digital twins and agentic twins. Virtual cells generate synthetic cellular states and predict responses from population data. Digital twins link models to specific biological counterparts, enabling longitudinal updating and prospective prediction. Agentic twins add spatial context, biologically constrained interactions and actions, and environmental feedback, enabling personalized, dynamic and interactive representations of cellular ecosystems. This narrative review is based on literature acquired from PubMed, Web of Science, bioRxiv and arXiv searches up to October 2026. AI-powered virtual cells could support drug discovery as foundation models that transfer biological knowledge across tasks, including data-limited settings. Their value depends on faithful extrapolation beyond training data and prospective validation against biological observations. Coupling these models to repeatedly measured experimental systems could enable personalized prediction, iterative updating and prioritization of perturbations, targets and therapeutic strategies.

records.title: FeDx-SF@βE assembly for AML treatment via GATA1/SLC40A1 pathway-mediated iron homeostasis disorder.
records.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. Inducing ferroptosis in AML cells represents a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, transcriptomic analyses first revealed that ferroptosis-associated transcriptional states were closely associated with prognosis and ex vivo drug-response heterogeneity in AML, providing a rationale for ferroptosis-oriented therapeutic design. Based on these findings, and further supported by a transcriptome-based target-scoring strategy, β-elemene (βE), a clinically used natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine, was selected as a candidate ferroptosis-related agent. We subsequently developed a nanodelivery system, designated FeDx-SF@βE, based on alcohol-induced silk fibroin (SF) folding to co-deliver ferric dextran (FeDx) and βE. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited a uniform particle size of 182.3 nm, favorable colloidal stability, and sustained drug release behavior. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient cellular uptake of FeDx-SF@βE by AML cells, leading to significantly inhibited cell viability. Pharmacological cell-death inhibitor rescue experiments showed that ferrostatin-1 produced the most pronounced protective effect, indicating that FeDx-SF@βE-induced AML cell death was predominantly ferroptosis-dependent. Mechanistically, βE-containing treatment suppressed the nuclear translocation of the transcription factor GATA1 and downregulated the iron efflux channel SLC40A1. GATA1/SLC40A1 gain- and loss-of-function analyses further demonstrated that activation of this axis attenuated FeDx-SF@βE-induced iron overload and ferroptotic injury, whereas suppression of this axis promoted intracellular iron retention, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage. In combination with FeDx-derived iron supply, βE-mediated inhibition of the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-export axis resulted in intracellular iron overload, glutathione depletion, ROS accumulation, extensive lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. Bulk transcriptomic and virtual-cell analyses further supported the involvement of the GATA1/SLC40A1 axis in ferroptosis-associated AML states and linked βE-related transcriptional programs to this regulatory mechanism. In a disseminated AML xenograft model, FeDx-SF@βE exhibited enhanced antileukemic efficacy and favorable biosafety. Collectively, this work provides a combined ferroptosis-oriented nanotherapeutic strategy for AML treatment and highlights the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-homeostasis axis as a functionally relevant mechanism for ferroptosis-targeted nanomedicine design.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence-Aided Design of Peptides with Custom Secondary Structure Motifs and Reduced Amino Acid Alphabets.
records.abstract: Proteins are highly diverse functional polymers where the specific sequence of amino acids, selected from a standard genetically encoded alphabet of 20 (C20), determines the structure and ultimately the function of the resulting folded protein. This standard alphabet has been identified to be nonrandomly distributed in physicochemical properties crucial to both structure formation and function, often referred to as coverage theory. While machine learning models have drastically improved protein structure prediction, success of protein design models lags structure prediction, particularly for custom secondary structure motifs and amino acid alphabets. Here, we therefore bridge contemporary biological theory with recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) to develop and evaluate a generative AI protein design model, trained on hundreds of thousands of proteins within the RCSB PDB, for custom secondary structure motifs using reduced amino acid alphabets (RAAs). Results indicate an overall success in designing novel proteins with desired secondary structure motifs for a broad range of amino acid alphabets and complexity of designs. Interestingly, for a substantial fraction of designs, ESMFold predicts a fold close to that of the target structure despite training only on physicochemical sequence space and secondary structure information. The development of this model advances research across multiple disciplines, from general scientific AI architecture development to protein design for biotechnology, astrobiology, and early-Earth evolutionary biology.

records.title: Aligning Molecules and Fragments in a Shared Embedding Space for Property-Aware Fragment Selection.
records.abstract: Fragment-based molecular design offers a chemically grounded strategy for exploring drug-like chemical space, yet identifying fragments that are both chemically feasible and relevant to a target property remains challenging. Fragment-level attribution is inherently ambiguous because each molecule contains multiple fragments and the same fragment can occur in molecular contexts with different property values. We introduce Molecule-Fragment Representation Alignment for Generation (M-FRAG), a property-aware framework that aligns molecules and fragments in a shared embedding space. M-FRAG organizes fragments according to their local relationships with parent molecules and their global distribution across molecular properties. Candidate fragments are then prioritized by their distance and distributional proximity to property-relevant molecular regions and used to guide reinforcement-learning-based molecular assembly. Across five docking-based multiobjective optimization tasks, M-FRAG improves the novel hit ratio by up to 58.00% over the strongest locally evaluated primary baseline and achieves the best Novel Top-5% docking scores for all five targets while maintaining strong novelty and chemical validity. These results establish embedding-space-guided fragment selection as an effective and traceable strategy for property-optimized molecular generation.

records.title: Reinforcement Learning for Aligning Structure-Based Molecular Generation toward Make-on-Demand Chemical Spaces.
records.abstract: Generative models for structure-based drug design have strong potential to accelerate early-stage drug discovery by enabling the conditional generation of target-specific molecules. However, a major bottleneck is that generated compounds are frequently difficult or impossible to synthesize, limiting their direct experimental validation and utility. We address this by optimizing for membership in make-on-demand chemical libraries, ensuring that generated molecules can be directly purchased and tested. To this end, we apply reinforcement learning to a pocket-conditioned generative molecular model, steering generated molecules toward two large make-on-demand spaces: Enamine REAL and Freedom 4.0. We compare an offline, preference-based strategy (direct preference optimization, DPO) and an online RL strategy (DiffusionNFT) across single-target and multi-target settings. In single-target optimization for KRAS, the fraction of unique purchasable candidates rises from 10.0% to 25.5% for Enamine REAL and from 4.3% to 12.1% for Freedom 4.0, while drug-likeness and docking-based affinity proxies are preserved. In multi-target optimization, DPO achieves consistent improvements across diverse protein targets, including a 23-fold increase for the challenging CDK4 pocket. These results demonstrate that RL alignment can substantially improve the experimental accessibility of SBDD candidates without sacrificing structural or chemical quality.

records.title: Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states.
records.abstract: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) mediate precise ligand-specific signaling profiles, yet structural visualization of how ligands alter receptor conformational landscapes in the absence of signaling partners or mimetics has proven challenging. Here we show that by combining generative protein design with deep-learning based ensemble prediction we can reliably design fiducial markers to facilitate cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) of GPCRs at arbitrary fusion points, enabling the visualization of previously intractable states. We validate the approach with high-throughput determination of inactive state structures of four pharmaceutically relevant GPCRs, allowing for key details of receptor pharmacology to be resolved in each case. We then engineered an extracellular fiducial marker for the prototypical β2-adrenergic receptor that enabled direct structural characterization of the rearrangement of key intracellular motifs in the absence of G-protein. Comparison with recent co-folding models highlights major gaps in current methods for predicting ligand-induced GPCR conformations. These results present a generalizable framework for accessing traditionally inaccessible structural states of small, dynamic proteins.

records.title: Augmenting the CATH database: a synthetic protein database for training biophysical-aware inverse folding models.
records.abstract: The three-dimensional structure of proteins is a fundamental determinant of their functional roles; however, biophysical properties such as stability, flexibility, and solubility are also critical for the experimental applicability of designed proteins. The generation of protein sequences capable of folding into a desired three-dimensional structure is known as the protein inverse folding problem and represents one of the fundamental computational challenges in protein engineering because of the vast search space involved. Current deep learning-based inverse folding models effectively learn structure-sequence relationships; however, these models largely overlook biophysical properties such as solubility and stability. This is primarily because these models are predominantly trained on natural protein datasets, and although natural proteins are highly efficient in cellular processes, they may not necessarily represent suitable candidates for experimental applications. In this study, 21,668 protein sequences from the CATH 4.3 database that passed the quality-filtering criteria were subjected to multi-objective optimization for stability, solubility, and flexibility using the Heuristic Metropolis-Hastings Optimization (HMHO) approach, resulting in the construction of a biophysically enriched synthetic protein dataset. To evaluate the effect of the data-centric approach independently of model architecture, the PiFold architecture was kept unchanged, and the baseline model trained on natural CATH sequences (PiFold) was compared with the model retrained on the optimized training data (PiFoldOPT) using natural CATH test sequences that had not been modified by HMHO. In accordance with the primary objective of the study, an initial set of 200 proteins was selected from the natural CATH test set using proportional stratified sampling that preserved the protein length distribution, with the aim of evaluating the biophysical properties of model-generated sequences on a representative test subset. In paired analyses conducted on 155 common proteins successfully designed by both models, PiFoldOPT designs exhibited markedly lower instability index values and higher predicted solubility than PiFold designs ([Formula: see text] for both comparisons; effect sizes [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text], respectively). Furthermore, the proportion of designs classified as stable increased from 65% for PiFold to 81% for PiFoldOPT. To evaluate these biophysical gains together with potential changes in inverse folding performance, sequence-level metrics were also compared on the natural test set. PiFoldOPT maintained sequence recovery performance close to that of the baseline model (0.4270 vs. 0.4286), while showing a limited but systematic reduction in prediction confidence (0.3779 vs. 0.3932). ESM-2-based zero-shot sequence scoring, performed to provide an evaluation independent of the biophysical prediction tools used during optimization, further showed that PiFoldOPT designs achieved more favorable protein language model scores for the majority of proteins. Finally, to evaluate whether the biophysical improvements compromised structural integrity, the initial 200-protein test subset selected using proportional stratified sampling that preserved the protein length distribution was used. Within this subset, 161 proteins for which ESMFold structure predictions were successfully obtained for the natural sequence, the PiFold design, and the PiFoldOPT design were included in the paired structural analysis. To minimize method-dependent comparison bias, all sequences across the three groups were evaluated using the same ESMFold structure prediction protocol. Using structures predicted from the natural sequences as references, PiFold and PiFoldOPT designs exhibited mean TM-scores of 0.784 and 0.792, RMSD values of 2.17 and 2.13 Å, and pLDDT values of 66.34 and 66.37, respectively. In addition to paired statistical comparisons, equivalence and non-inferiority analyses supported that the biophysical gains achieved with PiFoldOPT were not associated with a meaningful loss of predicted three-dimensional structural integrity. Taken together, these results demonstrate that biophysically guided training data enable the design of more stable and soluble protein sequences without modifying the model architecture. These findings reveal that, in protein inverse folding, not only model architecture but also the biophysical composition of the training data is an important determinant of design behavior, and demonstrate that biophysically enriched datasets represent a complementary data-centric strategy for protein design.

records.title: Deep learning-guided de novo design and molecular dynamics validation of putative glucocorticoid receptor binders.
records.abstract: Glucocorticoid receptor (GR) ligands are widely used anti-inflammatory agents, but their therapeutic utility is limited by severe adverse effects associated with long-term administration, including metabolic disorders, osteoporosis, and suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis. The discovery of structurally novel GR binders with improved safety profiles therefore remains a high-priority goal in drug development. In this purely computational study, a deep learning-guided de novo design framework based on maximum-likelihood training and transfer learning was developed to construct a focused library of 1,322 GR-relevant molecular entities. These molecules were initially screened using an ECFP4-based random forest (RF) classifier optimized for predicting GR activity, followed by docking-based virtual screening against the GR ligand-binding domain (LBD; PDB 4P6W). Five candidates were then prioritized on the basis of their binding profiles; however, their computed binding affinities remained substantially lower than that of the reference agonist mometasone furoate (MOF).Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations (500 ns × 3 independent replicates) were performed to evaluate complex stability, and MM/GBSA binding free-energy calculations further corroborated the binding profile. In silico ADME/toxicity profiling indicated favorable drug-like properties for the prioritized candidates. Overall, among the generated compounds, CPD_263 and CPD_313 achieve the best balance between predicted binding strength and safety-related parameters, emerging as computationally prioritized putative GR binders that merit subsequent experimental validation. All findings are computational and are intended to provide testable hypotheses for future experimental validation. Molecular generation was performed using a recurrent neural network trained by maximum-likelihood pretraining followed by target-specific transfer learning. Activity prediction employed an ECFP4-based random forest classifier. Molecular docking was implemented with AutoDock Vina, and MD simulations were performed using GROMACS 2022.5 to assess the dynamic stability of the hit candidates. Binding free energies were calculated with MM/GBSA, and in silico ADMET predictions were performed using SwissADME and ProTox-3.0.

records.title: Pan-cancer ctDNA panel and PET/CT in predicting true disease status after curative-intent treatment of head and neck cancer: a preliminary study.
records.abstract: Early detection of minimal residual disease is essential in managing head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), and positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) has been the standard imaging modality. Liquid biopsy (LB) of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has been introduced as a complementary method to enhance its diagnostic performance. The study aimed to investigate the performance of a pan-cancer ctDNA panel in conjunction with conventional PET/CT in the treatment response assessment. Patient/material and methods: Thirty-four patients with newly diagnosed HNSCC were prospectively enrolled, and 17 patients completed the study protocol. All patients underwent standard [18F]FDG-PET/CT imaging and a single timepoint LB 3 months after completion of definitive oncological treatment. A commercially available pan-cancer assay was utilized for ctDNA detection and tissue genomic analysis. Statistical assessments were performed separately for pathogenic variants of ctDNA detected concordantly in tissue and LB and for all detected pathogenic variants of ctDNA. The combination of ctDNA detection of concordant variants and PET/CT imaging contributed to the highest diagnostic accuracy in predicting true disease status. Sensitivity was highest for the combination of ctDNA detection of all variants and PET/CT imaging. Recurrence-free and overall survival were higher in patients having a negative LB in assessments of concordant variants when compared to those with a positive LB (p < 0.001 for both). A single-timepoint ctDNA detection with pan-cancer assay combined with PET/CT appears as a promising method for predicting true disease status in HNSCC. Our findings are presented as hypothesis generating due to the limited sample size.

records.title: Single-Vesicle Analysis, Spatial Deconvolution and Functional Circuit Mapping in Extracellular Vesicle Biology.
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles encode a universal language of intercellular communication-the 'ommunicome'-yet clinical translation has been constrained by extreme EV heterogeneity and the inability to trace circulating mRNA to its cellular origin. This review synthesizes three paradigm-shifting innovations that overcome these barriers: (1) the SCOPE platform, a CRISPR-Cas13/hybridization chain reaction system achieving single-molecule sensitivity at single-vesicle resolution; (2) computational spatial deconvolution enabling non-invasive, cell-type-resolved phenotyping of inaccessible tissues from standard biofluid samples and (3) the Functional Communication Circuits (FCC) framework-a network-based paradigm proposing that EV diagnostic power resides in correlated network relationships rather than isolated biomarkers. We critically evaluate SCOPE against competing technologies, establish its unique diagnostic niche and present clinical validation across oncology, neurology and cardiology. The FCC framework resolves the stoichiometric paradox of EV biology by demonstrating that low per-vesicle cargo copy numbers aggregate across the circulating EV pool to generate statistically robust population-level correlation signals. A translational roadmap encompasses pre-analytical standardization (including MISEV guidelines), targeted immunoaffinity enrichment and clinically actionable EV Communication Scores that distil multi-omics complexity into interpretable metrics. Five unresolved challenges, including the L1CAM controversy in neural EV isolation, SCOPE multiplexing limits and the absence of prospective FCC validation cohorts, are identified with concrete experimental solutions. The convergence of single-vesicle analysis, spatial deconvolution and functional circuit modelling is hypothesized to transform liquid biopsy from passive detection into active, systems-level interrogation of human disease.

records.title: Multi-analyte liquid biopsy characterization of metastatic inflammatory breast cancer: comparison with non-inflammatory breast cancer.
records.abstract: Inflammatory breast cancer (IBC) is a rare, aggressive disease with poorly understood biology. To provide a comprehensive characterization of blood-based biomarkers in IBC, we retrospectively analyzed 341 metastatic breast cancer patients (83 IBC, 258 non-IBC). Circulating tumor cells (CTCs), CTC clusters, cytokeratin + /CD45+ cells (DPcells), and tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (tdEVs) were evaluated. Matched circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) data were available for 59 IBC and 110 non-IBC. Analyte distributions and overall survival (OS) association were compared by IBC status. Circulating cellular analytes showed similar distributions, except for lower tdEVs in IBC. CTCs and tdEVs were associated with OS irrespective of IBC status, whereas DPcells only in IBC. TP53 (63%), PIK3CA (29%), and MYC (17%) were the most frequently altered genes in IBC. TP53 sequence variants (SVs; SNVs/indels) and CCNE1/MYC CNVs were enriched in IBC, but after adjusting for confounders, only PIK3CA SVs remained significantly less frequent. Network analysis identified TP53 SVs as key node in IBC, co-occurring with a CNV module (MYC/CCNE1/PIK3CA/FGFR1) with higher centrality in IBC than non-IBC. In multivariable analyses, PIK3CA and MYC CNVs were associated with worse OS. A clinical-ctDNA model showed strong prognostic performance, validated in an independent IBC cohort (n = 39). Overall, integrated liquid biopsy profiling unveiled distinct IBC features and identified prognostic biomarkers.

records.title: Diagnostic value of tumor-educated platelet transcriptomics in cancer: a systematic review of technical considerations and diagnostic accuracy.
records.abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and the search for noninvasive markers for cancer screening and diagnosis, as well as for patient monitoring, is of utmost importance to better and earlier detect cancer. As the second most abundant cell type in the bloodstream, platelets interact bidirectionally with cancer cells, acquiring cancer-associated molecular alterations that modify their transcriptomic profile and give rise to so-called tumor-educated platelets (TEPs). As an easily accessible and abundant blood component, TEPs have emerged as a promising liquid biopsy source for cancer diagnostic biomarkers. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the clinical utility of the TEP transcriptome as a potential source of diagnostic biomarkers in solid and hematological neoplasias. It also identifies the major challenges and future perspectives for their clinical implementation. The review protocol was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO: CRD42024486960).

records.title: Early Detection of Ovarian Cancer: Current Strategies and Future Directions.
records.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a major cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, mainly because most cases are diagnosed at advanced stages due to non-specific early symptoms. Although early detection is essential for improving clinical outcomes, accurate and accessible screening remains a major challenge, owing to the non-specific nature of early symptoms, the pronounced histological and molecular heterogeneity of the disease, and the poor performance of conventional screening approaches based on cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) and imaging modalities. This review outlines the major biological and technical challenges in the early diagnosis of OC, briefly summarizes the value and limitations of conventional diagnostic approaches and focuses on current progress in emerging biomarkers, including circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA)/cell-free DNA (cfDNA) alterations, exosomal biomarkers and mesothelin multi-marker combined detection strategies, and novel technologies, such as artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, single-cell sequencing and biosensors for early detection. We also discuss the advantages, current limitations, practical considerations and translational barriers of these approaches. Future advances in OC screening will require the integration of sensitive biomarkers, multimodal detection strategies and more accessible, cost-effective technologies to improve early diagnosis and patient survival.
